evals.query: I'm building a Kora HTTP API. Create a JSON request DTO UserRequest with name and email, and a UserResponse with id, name, email, createdAt.
expected_behavior: Annotates each DTO type with @Json imported from io.koraframework.json.common.annotation
Uses Java records (or Kotlin data classes) for the DTOs
Adds annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" and implementation "io.koraframework:json-common" (Kotlin: ksp "io.koraframework:symbol-processors")
Uses the platform "io.koraframework:kora-bom" at version 2.0.0.RC2 (koraVersion property) rather than pinning per-artifact versions
Notes that the @KoraApp interface must extend io.koraframework.json.common.JsonModule
Does not use foreign @JsonProperty or field injection; uses constructor injection
anti_behavior: Writes the artifact ru.tinkoff.kora:json-module or io.koraframework:json-module
Writes the BOM ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent
Imports ru.tinkoff.kora.json.common.annotation.Json
Pins 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT, 2.0.0.alpha6 or a 1.x version as the version for a new project

evals.query: Our Kora 1.x service depends on ru.tinkoff.kora:json-module and its @KoraApp extends ru.tinkoff.kora.json.module.JsonModule. What are the Kora 2.0 equivalents?
expected_behavior: States the artifact is io.koraframework:json-common — json-module does not exist in Kora 2.0
States the module interface is io.koraframework.json.common.JsonModule (package .common, not .module)
States that JsonCommonModule was folded into JsonModule and no longer exists
Mentions the BOM change ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent -> io.koraframework:kora-bom
Notes that json-common should be declared explicitly in every Gradle module using @Json
anti_behavior: Claims io.koraframework:json-module or io.koraframework.json.module.JsonModule exists
Recommends keeping JsonCommonModule
Suggests running a blind package find/replace as the whole migration

evals.query: Set up a fresh Gradle module that uses Kora 2.0 JSON. Which Kora version and which repositories do I declare?
expected_behavior: Pins koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 — the released Kora 2.0 version on Maven Central
Uses plain mavenCentral(); no extra repository is needed for a released 2.0.0.RC2
Declares platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") and no per-artifact versions
Adds io.koraframework:json-common plus annotation-processors (Java) or symbol-processors (Kotlin)
If 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT is mentioned at all, labels it the master development line and pairs it with https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots
anti_behavior: Uses 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT as the version for a new project
Uses 2.0.0.alpha6 or claims Central only publishes an alpha
Adds a custom/snapshot repository for the 2.0.0.RC2 release
Offers a leftover Central artifact such as kora-parent or cache-redis, which the 2.0 BOM does not constrain

evals.query: Migrating to Kora 2.0: my code calls jsonWriter.toByteArrayUnchecked(dto), jsonWriter.toStringUnchecked(dto) and jsonReader.readUnchecked(bytes). These methods no longer resolve.
expected_behavior: Maps toByteArrayUnchecked -> toByteArray, toStringUnchecked -> toString, readUnchecked -> read
States that the surviving methods declare no checked exception — only the unchecked tools.jackson.core.JacksonException
Warns that a leftover try/catch (IOException) around toByteArray is now a Java compile error ("exception IOException is never thrown in body of corresponding try statement")
Says to delete the now-unused import java.io.IOException
anti_behavior: Keeps or reintroduces a *Unchecked method
Keeps the try/catch (IOException) or suggests catching IOException
Claims the plain methods still throw IOException

expected_behavior: Identifies the error as "exception IOException is never thrown in body of corresponding try statement"
Explains that JsonWriter.toByteArray(@Nullable T) declares no checked exception in Kora 2.0 — only the unchecked tools.jackson.core.JacksonException
Rewrites the snippet as a single unguarded return statement
Removes the java.io.IOException import
anti_behavior: Suggests catching Exception or IOException anyway
Suggests adding throws IOException to the enclosing method
Claims the method signature is unchanged from Kora 1.x

evals.query: In my Kotlin Kafka listener on Kora 2.0, `val event: OrderEvent = reader.read(record.value())` fails to compile with a type mismatch. Why, and how do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Explains that JsonReader<T>.read(...) is annotated @Nullable in Kora 2.0, so it returns T?
Fixes it with requireNotNull(reader.read(data)) (or an explicit null check / !!)
Notes that reading the JSON literal null legitimately yields null, so a null check is real logic rather than ceremony
Does not change the declared type of the JsonReader component
anti_behavior: Claims read() returns a non-null type
Suggests a platform-type cast or an unsafe unchecked cast
Suggests switching to a suspend or reactive reader API

evals.query: Add a Kora @HttpController UserController with a POST /users that takes a JSON body and a GET /users/{id} that returns JSON.
expected_behavior: Marks the request parameter with @Json and the route method with @Json
Uses @HttpRoute(method = HttpMethod.POST/GET, path = ...) and @Path for the id
Annotates the controller with @HttpController and @Component, injecting the service via the constructor
Puts @Json on the DTO types themselves, not only on the controller parameter
Uses synchronous return types — no Mono/Flux/CompletionStage/suspend
Does not use @RestController, @RequestBody, @GetMapping or @PathVariable

evals.query: My JSON uses snake_case keys like user_id and first_name, and some fields are optional. How do I map this in a Kora 2.0 DTO?
expected_behavior: Uses @JsonField("user_id") to rename individual fields
Mentions @NamingStrategy(SnakeCaseNameConverter.class) as the wholesale alternative
Marks optional fields with JSpecify org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable (Kotlin: nullable type T?)
Explains that all fields are required by default
For a qualified/nested Java type, places the type-use @Nullable before the simple name (java.util.@Nullable List<String>)
Does not introduce com.fasterxml.jackson @JsonProperty
anti_behavior: Uses javax/jakarta @Nullable or invents a Kora @Nullable
Writes @Nullable java.util.List<String> in a position javac rejects
Uses @field:Nullable in Kotlin

evals.query: Create a polymorphic JSON result PaymentResult with a discriminator field type and two cases PaymentSuccess (SUCCESS) and PaymentError (ERROR).
expected_behavior: Defines a sealed interface annotated with @Json and @JsonDiscriminatorField("type")
Annotates EVERY subtype with its own @Json — otherwise the sealed mapper cannot be wired
Annotates each subtype with @JsonDiscriminatorValue matching the JSON value
Does not add a redundant String type component to the subtypes, or, if it adds one, maps its JSON name onto the discriminator field
Does not use Jackson @JsonTypeInfo/@JsonSubTypes
anti_behavior: Claims the discriminator must be declared as a record component on every subtype
Omits @Json from the subtypes
Claims @JsonDiscriminatorValue is mandatory (it defaults to the subtype simple name)

evals.query: I have a PATCH /users/{id} endpoint that must distinguish a field omitted from the body from a field explicitly set to null. How do I model the request DTO in Kora?
expected_behavior: Uses io.koraframework.json.common.JsonNullable<T> for the patchable fields
Reads state with isDefined() and value() (and isNull() when needed), not Optional-style isPresent()/get()
Explains the three states: defined non-null, defined null, undefined (omitted)
Notes that JsonNullable.undefined() is omitted from the output even under @JsonInclude(ALWAYS)
Does not invent isAbsent()/isPresent() methods on JsonNullable

evals.query: I need to serialize LocalDate as dd.MM.yyyy across my Kora 2.0 app. Register a custom JSON mapper.
expected_behavior: Provides JsonReader<LocalDate> and JsonWriter<LocalDate> factories in a @Module (io.koraframework.common.annotation.Module) or directly in @KoraApp
Uses PLAIN factory methods, explaining that a non-default component overrides JsonModule's @DefaultComponent built-in
Uses the Jackson 3 API: tools.jackson.core.JsonParser/JsonGenerator, parser.getString()/getValueAsString(), generator.writeString/writeNull, StreamReadException for failures
Handles null in the writer (writeNull) and returns null for JsonToken.VALUE_NULL in the reader
Builds the DateTimeFormatter once, outside the lambda
Mentions @Mapping(X.class) as the per-field alternative
anti_behavior: Uses parser.getText(), generator.writeStringField(...) or writeFieldName(...) (Jackson 2 API)
Imports com.fasterxml.jackson.* types
Throws or catches IOException
Marks the override with @DefaultComponent, leaving two competing defaults

evals.query: Create an OrderStatus enum that serializes to lowercase strings like pending and shipped in a Kora @Json DTO, and another that serializes to an integer code.
expected_behavior: Annotates both enums with @Json
For the string case, overrides toString() to return the lowercase value
Explains that the default value accessor is toString() and the reader matches back through the same accessor
For the integer case, exposes a public zero-argument accessor annotated @Json whose return type becomes the JSON value type
Does not add a fromString/valueOf helper and claim Kora uses it
Does not use fasterxml enum annotations

evals.query: My team has an existing Jackson ObjectMapper config. How do I make a Kora 2.0 app route its HTTP JSON bodies through Jackson?
expected_behavior: Extends io.koraframework.json.jackson.module.JacksonModule on the @KoraApp interface
Adds implementation "io.koraframework:jackson-module"
States that jackson-module binds Jackson 3 under the group tools.jackson.core (jackson-databind 3.x) and that the mapper type is tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper
States that jackson-databind arrives transitively via jackson-module's api dependency, so the consumer must NOT add a Jackson coordinate of their own
States that JacksonModule supplies NO ObjectMapper — the app must provide one as a component, or the graph fails with "No component found for dependency tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper"
Clarifies that JacksonModule replaces only the HTTP request/response body mappers, not JsonReader/JsonWriter generation, so @Json and json-common are still needed
Notes that the Kora-native HTTP JSON mappers are @DefaultComponent, so JacksonModule's plain factories take precedence automatically
anti_behavior: Adds com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind or imports com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper
Registers a Jackson 2 add-on such as jackson-datatype-jsr310 or jackson-module-kotlin against a tools.jackson ObjectMapper
Claims Kora supplies a default ObjectMapper that a factory merely overrides
Claims JacksonModule replaces the generated JsonReader/JsonWriter components
Tells the user to add tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind explicitly alongside jackson-module

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 build fails with: No component found for dependency io.koraframework.json.common.JsonReader<com.example.OrderEvent>. What did I miss?
expected_behavior: Checks that OrderEvent carries @Json (or @JsonReader) on the type itself
Checks that the @KoraApp interface extends io.koraframework.json.common.JsonModule
Checks that io.koraframework:json-common and the annotation processor (annotation-processors / symbol-processors) are on the module's classpath
For a sealed type, checks that every subtype carries its own @Json
Mentions that stale generated sources from a 1.x rename need ./gradlew clean --no-build-cache rather than hand-editing build/generated
anti_behavior: Suggests registering the DTO in a reflection config or a runtime mapper registry
Suggests annotating only the controller parameter
Suggests editing generated sources under build/

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 HTTP endpoint receives an Order JSON. When clients send bad input we want to return a helpful 400. What do Kora's generated JSON readers throw, and what does the message look like for a wrong type, a missing field or an unknown sealed-type discriminator?
expected_behavior: States that generated and built-in readers throw tools.jackson.core.exc.StreamReadException (unchecked), which a handler can map to 400
Describes the message shape "Failed to read json <Type>[.<field>]: expected <what>, but got <actual> (at <JSON pointer>)", with <root> for the top level
Gives the missing-field form "Failed to read json <Type>: missing required field(s): a, b" and the null form "<Type>.<field>: required field must not be null"
Gives the sealed-type forms: "missing required discriminator field \"type\", expected one of [...]" and "unknown discriminator value \"x\" for field \"type\", expected one of [...]"
Recommends not parsing the message text for control flow
anti_behavior: Quotes the old token-dump messages such as "Expecting VALUE_STRING token, got ..." as Kora's current output
Claims the reader throws a checked IOException or a Kora-specific JSON exception type
Claims defaultValue on @JsonDiscriminatorField also absorbs unknown discriminator values

evals.query: In Kora 2.0 I have a value type `record UserId(long id)` and want it to appear in JSON as a bare number (e.g. `"owner": 42`) wherever it is used in my @Json DTOs, like Jackson's @JsonCreator(DELEGATING) + @JsonValue. How?
expected_behavior: Annotates a public static factory `@JsonReader public static UserId of(long v)` and a value method `@JsonWriter public long id()` (or a static `(UserId) -> long` @JsonWriter method) on the type
Explains that the processor then generates a delegating JsonReader/JsonWriter that reads/writes the long through JsonReader<Long>/JsonWriter<Long>
For Kotlin, places the @JsonReader factory in the companion object
Notes that a factory that is not public static is rejected ("@JsonReader factory method must be public static")
Does not write a hand-rolled custom JsonReader/JsonWriter module as the only option and does not use Jackson's @JsonCreator/@JsonValue
anti_behavior: Claims Kora cannot serialize a non-enum type as a single value
Uses @JsonValue or @JsonCreator from com.fasterxml or tools.jackson annotations
